title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore East on 1968-06-14

ai_review.summary: Ragged audience tape but a landmark 1968 performance with a smoking St. Stephen/Eleven sequence and wild feedback sandwich.
ai_review.review: The show is widely hailed as one of the most important 1968 concerts, highlighted by an incendiary St. Stephen that rides a scorching Eleven and unusual transitions like Alligator into Lovelight.  Recording quality is consistently described as low‑fidelity audience tape – clipped vocals and muddy mix – yet many listeners report it becomes enjoyable with good headphones.  The performance’s historic value outweighs the technical flaws.

ai_rating.rationale: Reviewers praise the musical performance (standout sequences, historic set) while repeatedly noting poor recording fidelity; weighted average yields a solid 4‑star rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Low‑fidelity AUD tape with clipping, barely audible vocals and ragged mix; some reviewers note occasional clarity when listened to on headphones.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Features a rare ‘feedback sandwich’ (opening and closing feedback) with the sequence Feedback → The Eleven → St. Stephen, plus an unusual Alligator → Lovelight transition; overall flow described as historic and uniquely thrilling.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s lead guitar is described as blazing and carries the performance; his vocals are highlighted despite being hard to hear on the tape.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil’s bass fills and occasional vocal contributions are noted, though limited by recording quality.
